data.long_meaning: Derived from the name Anas ibn Malik, meaning the supporter or helper. A name for a boy who is kind, loyal, and always there to support and help those around him. The name Anasat carries the meaning “Supporter, Helper” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Anasat usually hope their child will grow to embody supporter, helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Anasat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Supporter, Helper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anasat total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The Islamic name Anas is one that holds a significant cultural impact, as it is named after one of the most important and beloved companions of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), Anas ibn Malik. Anas was known for his exceptional memory, honesty, and willingness to help and support both the Prophet (PBUH) and the Islamic community as a whole. Due to his close association with the Prophet (PBUH), Anas played a critical role in transmitting and preserving hadiths (traditions of the Prophet). Therefore, the name Anas is often given to boys as a reminder to uphold these qualities and strive to support and help others just as Anas ibn Malik did.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the Islamic name Anas is rooted in the Prophetic tradition and the virtues of Anas ibn Malik. Anas' unwavering dedication to the Prophet (PBUH) and the Islamic community demonstrates a crucial aspect of faith: a strong sense of community and love for others. Furthermore, Anas' exceptional memory and his role in preserving the traditions of the Prophet remind us of the importance of knowledge and wisdom in our spiritual growth. By giving the name Anas to a boy, we are encouraging him to embody these traits and strive to support and help others while fostering a deep love for knowledge and wisdom.

historical_references.reference: Anas ibn Malik (ra) was a prominent Sahabi (companion) of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) who is known for his extensive knowledge of Hadith. He was born in the city of Tan'im, in the tribe of Qais, in central Arabia around 8-10 BH (Before Hijrah/Common Era) and grew up in Makkah. He migrated to Medina with the Prophet (pbuh) in 1 AH (After Hijrah/Islamic Calendar) and became one of the most trusted companions of the Prophet (pbuh), known for his loyalty, generosity, and memory.
historical_references.context: Sahabi, Companion of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), Knowledge of Hadith

historical_references.reference: Anas ibn Malik (ra) was also the governor of Kufa during the Umayyad Caliphate (661-750 AD). He was appointed by Caliph Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik and is remembered for his just and fair rule. During his governorship, he introduced various reforms aimed at improving the administrative and financial systems of the province. He is also known for his patronage of scholars and poets.
historical_references.context: Governor of Kufa, Reforms, Patronage of Scholars and Poets

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern context, the term 'Anasat' is used on various social media platforms such as Twitter, Reddit, and Facebook, to refer to individuals or groups who provide support or assistance to a cause or community. Similarly, an individual providing guidance or support to others online might be referred to as an Anasat. This usage highlights the importance of collective efforts and mutual support in achieving common goals and upholding shared values.
